To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Sma I and the ScaI mutations of ANP precursor genes are associated with sodium-sensitiveness of blood pressure in patients with essential arterial hypertension.
the Sma I and/or Sca I gene polymorphisms of ANP precursor are not associated with essential hypertension in Caucasians.
the frequencies of Sca I polymorphisms of ANP precursor genes are significantly higher in patients with sodium sensitive hypertension as compared to sodium non-sensitive hypertensives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the methods for the detection of Sma I and/or Sca I polymorphisms in the ANP gene and determination of their association with sodium-sensitivity in essential hypertension.
a new approach to the pathogenesis of hypertension and the development of new therapeutic strategies.
a new approach to the pathogenesis of sodium-sensitive hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic defect of ANP precursor may contribute to the development of essential hypertension in some populations.
the Sca I mutation is a genetic factor associated with sodium-susceptibility in hypertensives of Caucasian origin.
, in contrast with African-Americans, Sca I polymorphisms of ANP precursor genes are not a genetic factor in the development of essential hypertension in Caucasians.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Sca I mutation is a genetic marker for sodium-sensitive hypertension in Caucasians.
the Sma I and the Sca 1 polymorphisms in ANP precursor gene are not associated with essential hypertension in Caucasians.
the Sma I and/or Sca I mutations in the ANP gene may be one of the genetic factors predisposing to essential hypertension in sodium-sensitive patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Sca I gene polymorphism of the ANP gene may be a genetic marker for the development of sodium-sensitivity of hypertension in Caucasians.
Sca I polymorphisms of the ANP gene may be a marker of sodium-sensitivity of BP and the Sma I mutation may be a marker for sodium-nonsensitivity of BP in Caucasian population.
, in contrast with African-Americans, in Caucasian hypertensives, the Sca I mutation of ANP gene may be more important than Sma I polymorphisms.
